Fig. 7. Comparison in terms of valid extracted 128×128 patches (green), contaminated patches (orange) vs non-valid patches (red) in pseudo-anonymized configurations between the Naive Uniform Grid Method [12], Kochkarev et al. [13], PatchMatch [22] and our proposed Pseudo-Anonymized Contextual patch Extraction method, PACE. It can be observed that the proposed PACE captures higher patch density in residual sensitive areas without compromising general coverage of the whole ID image compared with the competing methods thanks to a greedy strategy that prioritizes coordinates adjacent to redacted areas.

Fig. 3. Proposed refined post-processing pipeline for text digital attacks. The GenAI pipeline (top, light-blue background) involves GenAI methods (Φtext) to synthesize the new text, while also removes the target text area (Φinpaint), creating Ibg . Finally, an alpha-blending operation αt from the extracted text mask is applied to embed the new content. The classical pipeline (bottom, light-green background) leverages the existing content (Isrc) along with the target text removed image (Ibg) and embeds the source content crop Tfake into the Itgt in a similar fashion as the GenAI pipeline (i.e., alpha-blending operation).
